scenarioStory.history: Roofing contractor fell approximately 25 feet from scaffolding onto packed dirt, landing feet-first then falling backward. Coworkers report he was briefly stunned but did not lose consciousness. Complains of severe pelvic pain and inability to stand. Denies neck pain but reports diffuse lower back tenderness.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 48-year-old male supine at the base of a scaffold, alert and in severe pain, with bruising and asymmetry over the pelvis. He denies neck pain but reports diffuse back and pelvic pain. → Primary survey and pelvic binder applied: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, palpates the pelvis once for instability, applies a pelvic binder, initiates spinal motion restriction given the fall greater than 10 feet, and establishes IV access for fluid resuscitation. → Fluid bolus given for shock: A 500 mL crystalloid bolus is given for persistent hypotension. Blood pressure improves toward the trauma resuscitation target, and the patient receives weight-based analgesia before transport. → Perfusion improved, prepared for transport: Patient is packaged with pelvic binder and cervical collar in place, perfusion trending toward target, and transported to a trauma center with serial vital sign reassessment.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Fall from scaffolding, severe pelvic and lower back pain

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 48-year-old male supine at the base of a scaffold, alert and in severe pain, with bruising and asymmetry over the pelvis. He denies neck pain but reports diffuse back and pelvic pain.

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey and pelvic binder applied
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, palpates the pelvis once for instability, applies a pelvic binder, initiates spinal motion restriction given the fall greater than 10 feet, and establishes IV access for fluid resuscitation.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey: hemorrhage, airway, breathing, circulation, head/hypothermia
Palpate pelvis ONCE by applying medial pressure on iliac crests bilaterally to assess instability
Apply pelvic binder to stabilize suspected unstable pelvis
Apply cervical collar and initiate spinal motion restriction for fall >10 feet
Establish large-bore IV access given SBP <90 and HR >120

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus given for shock
scenarioEvents.description: A 500 mL crystalloid bolus is given for persistent hypotension. Blood pressure improves toward the trauma resuscitation target, and the patient receives weight-based analgesia before transport.
relatedChecklist: 500 mL crystalloid bolus IV, reassess SBP, repeat as needed (target SBP 90 mmHg)
Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg x 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)

scenarioEvents.name: Perfusion improved, prepared for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged with pelvic binder and cervical collar in place, perfusion trending toward target, and transported to a trauma center with serial vital sign reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and pelvic binder position serially en route to trauma center
Transport to appropriate trauma center per field triage guideline; minimize scene time

scenarioEvents.name: Pelvis palpated repeatedly to reassess
scenarioEvents.description: The crew repeatedly presses on the pelvis to 'recheck' instability instead of palpating once, risking dislodgement of a forming clot. The patient's pain and hemodynamic status worsen.
relatedChecklist: Stop repeat pelvic palpation, apply binder immediately, and begin fluid resuscitation
